event.title: Meta Fined $567 Million for Child Safety Violations
event.canonical_title: Meta Fined $567 Million for Child Safety Violations
event.summary: A New Mexico judge has ordered Meta to pay $567 million due to findings that the company created a 'public nuisance' harming children's mental health. This ruling is part of ongoing legal actions against Meta regarding its impact on young users. The company plans to appeal the decision and has previously faced additional fines related to similar issues.

timeline.title: Meta Fined $942 Million for Failing to Protect Children Online
timeline.summary: Meta has been ordered to pay a total of $942 million after a US judge ruled the company failed to protect children from harm on its social media platforms. This penalty includes $567 million for creating a public nuisance and endangering children, alongside an additional $375 million already imposed. Meta plans to appeal the ruling, asserting its commitment to safeguarding young users.

event_overview.title: About Child Safety
event_overview.subject: Child Safety
event_overview.summary: This event concerns New Mexico’s civil case against Meta Platforms over alleged child-safety failures on Facebook, Instagram and related services. A jury found Meta liable under the state Unfair Practices Act in March 2026, and a subsequent court phase considered monetary and injunctive remedies; the August developments concern the resulting financial sanctions and required protections.

facts.label: Legal basis
facts.value: New Mexico alleged that Meta misled consumers about platform safety and endangered children; the March jury verdict found liability on both claims under the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act.

facts.label: Key dates and phases
facts.value: The jury returned its verdict on March 24, 2026. A second, judge-decided phase seeking public-nuisance relief and operational changes began on May 4 and concluded on May 22, 2026.

facts.label: Financial remedies
facts.value: The March verdict imposed $375 million in civil penalties. The later $567 million order reported in August was additional, bringing the reported combined financial amount to $942 million.

facts.label: Stated remedial focus
facts.value: The state sought platform changes for New Mexico users under 18, including age verification, safer recommendation systems, limits on adult-minor messaging, warning labels, permanent bans for accounts involved in exploitation, and independent oversight.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows the August 7–8, 2026 penalty and remedy developments in the New Mexico Meta case; it does not attempt to cover every separate lawsuit, regulatory inquiry, appeal, or broader child-online-safety policy debate involving Meta or other platforms.
